source: no published source; read from the installed 2.0.1 plugin.dylib and its res/ artwork

lines: A narrow blank panel carrying the Patch & Tweak name, with a hidden jack that spins its ampersand
Turns the red ampersand of the Patch & Tweak logo, a full turn for every 10V and the other way for negative voltage; the turn is held to a little over three revolutions a second
Note — the jack is drawn invisibly, so there is nothing on the panel to aim at, but a cable dropped on the spot takes hold and a patched cable shows against the artwork
Note — the panel passes no audio and puts nothing out; the only thing it does is turn the ampersand in time with whatever you patch

0.why: PatchAndTweak 2.0.1 plugin.dylib, BlankPanel::process at 0x23c0: the module's config call is config(0, 1, 0, 0); process reads the channels byte of input 0 as a connection test and then voltages[0] only, with no loop over channels. PatchAndTweak 2.0.1 plugin.dylib, BlankPanel::process at 0x23c0: voltages[0] is multiplied by 0x3e4ccccd (0.2f) and then by the double 3.14159265358979, and the result is slew-limited against the rates at Module+0x14c and Module+0x150, both set to 20.0f in the constructor at 0x2118; the angle at Module+0x154 is read by RotatableSVG::step and applied with nvgTransformRotate

Blank.notes: The maker never called configInput for this jack, so Rack's hover tooltip for it is blank and the census records it with no name. It is a real PortWidget added with addInput and it accepts a cable; the InvisiblePort constructor loads PJ301M.svg and then hides the drawn parts, leaving a jack that works and cannot be seen. A full turn at 10V follows from 0.2 times pi radians per volt; the three-revolutions figure is the 20.0 radians-per-second slew limit divided by two pi, and neither derived number is stored in the binary. The ampersand between PATCH and TWEAK is not part of the panel artwork: it is a separate rotating widget, which is why the panel SVG renders with a gap where it belongs.
